newsitem.title: UK: FLYING FLOWERS SOWING SEEDS FOR FUTURE.
newsitem.headline: FLYING FLOWERS SOWING SEEDS FOR FUTURE.

text.p: Britain's largest flower-by-post company, Flying Flowers Plc, said it was planning to achieve higher growth by diversifying its product range and expanding its glass-house area to feed demand.
Flying Flowers reported doubling of pre-tax profits in its six months to July 4, 1997 to 3.37 million stg on a turnover of 23.7 million on Wednesday.
The company's earnings per share rose to 11.33 pence a share from 6.15 p per share.
In a profit forecast for the current year, the company said it expected "substantial profits growth" in the second half of the year in line with expectations.
It also said its brokers had upgraded its pre-tax profit forecast to 7.7 million stg for the year to December 1998.
A bulk of its business comes from catering for special occasions including Valentines's Day, Christmas Day and Mother's Day.
The company's chairman Walter Goldsmith said it hoped to expand its bedding plants and perennials business.
Flying Flowers expects to get permission -- in the next 10 days -- to set up a new six acre glass house near its existing facilities in Jersey to cater to its bedding plants and perennials.
The company also has its sights on overseas markets.
"It is clearly an opportunity...," Goldsmith said. However, it will have to tackle postal problems in some of the potential markets in Europe and Asia.
The company may negotiate alliances with low-cost courier firms to develop an overseas market, it said.
